I run Ubuntu and I have been testing Veracrypt a bit. If I want to encrypt my hard drives or partitions that I use for data storage, do I need to copy the files partition by partition to some temporary storage, create a Veracrypt volume on the partition and then copy the files back? Am I thinking of doing this wrong? Is this the best software for the job?

How about if I want to encrypt my home folder?

Most linux distros have an option to encrypt the disks when installing them (using LUKS). If you want to use something else for a full disk encryption I would recommend backing up everything you don't want to accidentally lose first. As for Veracrypt they are still kind of new and have never been audited. Truecrypt 7,1a has however been heavily audited and there's no reason not to trust it. Either should be okay though (don't use anything past TC 7.1a!). For your home folder, you can make that a separate partition and encrypt that.
Veracrypt is a fork of truecrypt. So you can check the changes. I suppose?

Oh I know that, it's just still relativity new and hasn't gone through any intense security auditing yet. There are some great improvements too though when compared to Truecrypt (more PBKDF2-RIPEMD160 iterations, anyone?).

Personally I use LUKS for full disk, and vera/true for containers. I'm not going to rely on a single layer of protection regardless.

do I need to copy the files partition by partition to some temporary storage, create a Veracrypt volume on the partition and then copy the files back?

Yes, you need to move your existing files to a temporary partition and then either create an encrypted container large enough for all your files or encrypt the entire drive (Partition/device-hosted (non-system)).

How about if I want to encrypt my home folder?

LUKS is the way to go. See this document.

Edit: There's in-place encryption apparently (VeraCrypt). See https://veracrypt.codeplex.com/wikipage?title=System%20Encryption .
